caseResults.answer:
Incremental/full note: no prior review marker found for this diff — reviewing as `full` (single new feature: billing overdue notification). Diff-size gate: 14 + ~13 lines, well under any threshold — no slicing concern, reviewing in full. ## Review: billing overdue-notification + tests **Scope:** `src/billing/notify.ts` (new, 14 lines), `src/billing/notify.test.ts` (new, 2 tests). ### Findings | Severity | File:line | Evidence | Fix | |---|---|---|---| | P2 | `src/billing/notify.test.ts:5,11` | Test at line 5 asserts only `expect(mailer.send).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`; test at line 11 asserts only `.resolves.not.toThrow()`. Run the stub pass: replace `notifyOverdue`'s body with a no-op `async () => {}`. The line-5 test still passes (send is never called, by any invoice). The line-11 test still passes (a no-op resolves and never throws). Both new tests pass against a function that does nothing. | Neither test proves the one thing the feature exists to do — call `mailer.send` for an overdue invoice. Add a positive-assertion test, e.g. `it('sends notification for an overdue invoice', async () => { const mailer = { send: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined) }; await notifyOverdue([overdueInvoice], mailer); expect(mailer.send).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1); expect(mailer.send).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ id: overdueInvoice.id })); })`. | **Options for closing this (since it needs a choice about how, not whether):** - a) Add a third, dedicated "sends for overdue invoice" test with a positive `toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` assertion. Cheap, isolates the one missing invariant, doesn't touch the two existing tests. - b) Fold a positive assertion into the existing "survives a failing mailer" test (assert `mailer.send` was called *before* asserting the promise resolves) — covers "call happened" and "call failing doesn't propagate" in one test. - → I'd take **(a)**, because (a) and (b) test different invariants (selection logic vs. error containment); merging them means a future break in selection logic silently shows up as a failure in a test named "survives a failing mailer," which is a confusing signal to debug from. Keep them separate; (a) is one line added, not a rewrite. - Attack on (a): asserting exact invoice equality via `toHaveBeenCalledWith(overdueInvoice)` is brittle if the invoice shape grows extra fields later — prefer `expect.objectContaining({ id: overdueInvoice.id })` or just `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` if the identity isn't the thing under test. No other findings. `notifyOverdue` itself (lines 1–14) is straightforward and does what it says; I have no evidence of a defect in the implementation — the gap is entirely in test coverage, not in the 14 lines of logic. ### Observations - The "survives a failing mailer" test name promises more than it checks: it shows the returned promise doesn't reject, but nothing confirms the rejection was logged, swallowed intentionally, or otherwise handled rather than silently discarded. Not a Finding (no evidence of a concrete bad outcome, no repro) — worth a comment in the test or implementation if silent-swallow is unintentional. ### What this change does well - The implementation is small and single-purpose — one filter-and-send loop, easy to read in isolation. - The test file already exercises two real edges (paid invoices excluded; mailer failure doesn't crash the caller) rather than just a happy path — the gap is that neither edge is paired with the positive "it actually sends" case, not that the edges chosen are wrong. ### Docs `docs not checked` — no behaviour, flag, or public API name changed from an existing value (this is new surface, `notifyOverdue`); nothing to grep against in a prior document. ### Change map ```mermaid flowchart LR T["src/billing/notify.test.ts
(P2: no positive-call assertion)"] -->|await notifyOverdue| N[src/billing/notify.ts] N -->|mailer.send per overdue invoice| M[mailer.send mock] ``` ### Verdict P2 only, no P0/P1 — does not block `gate:code`. ``` $ bd create "Billing notify tests assert only negative outcomes, missing positive mailer.send call assertion (src/billing/notify.test.ts:5,11)" --type bug --priority 2 ``` ``` bash scripts/log-verdict.sh code-reviewer APPROVED auto feature=billing-overdue-notify review=docs/reviews/REVIEW-billing-overdue-notify.md finding=stub-pass-notify-tests ```
